why:
phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-17, first of three. rclcpp's `SubscriptionOptions` has no counterpart; RFC-0047's scheduling context is ours. NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089); this item has no upstream candidate, so there is nothing for a constraint to permit, weaken or refuse. Forcing one here would invent a decision about upstream that nobody made.

THE FINDING: the field is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE on the poll overload. The guard at `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/subscription.hpp:674` is `if (options.sched_context != SCHED_CONTEXT_UNSET && out.has_sched_handle())`, and `has_sched_handle()` is `sched_handle_id_ != SIZE_MAX`. That field defaults to `SIZE_MAX` and is assigned at exactly four sites (`:717`, `:750`, `:783`, `:830`), all four in the CALLBACK-mode creates. The poll create sets none, so the second conjunct is a compile-time-constant false for this overload.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG — the option is accepted, the call returns ok, and the entity runs on the default context. It is at least documented at the field (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/options.hpp:66`) and at the create (`subscription.hpp:656`), which is the difference between this and a trap; the row exists because a documented no-op is still a capability claimed by a name. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

AMENDED 2026-09-18 (phase-456 W2b). The finding stands and its mechanism changed: the unreachable second conjunct is GONE rather than still-false. The poll creator takes a `nros::PollSubscription<M>&`, a type with no `sched_handle_id_` and no `has_sched_handle()`, so `sched_context` on that overload is not a branch that cannot be taken but a field with nothing to bind, said so at the definition in `rclcpp/polling_subscription.hpp`. Still SILENTLY WRONG for a caller who sets it, and still documented at both ends; what a reader can no longer do is find a guard and believe it might fire.
